scheme_name: Scheme for Supply of Male Goat on Subsidy Basis
description:
The Scheme for Supply of Male Goat on Subsidy Basis was launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This scheme is part of the broader initiative to enhance the livelihoods of small and marginal farmers. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to improve the income levels of farmers through goat rearing. 

The scheme aims to provide quality male goats to enhance the breeding stock of local goats. 

This is expected to lead to better quality meat production and increased milk yield. 

The scheme specifically targets small and marginal farmers who are engaged in goat rearing. 

The government has set a target to provide male goats to at least 10,000 beneficiaries annually. 

The subsidy provided under this scheme is designed to make it financially viable for farmers to improve their livestock. 

Under this scheme, a subsidy of 50 percent of the cost of the male goat is provided. 

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 15,000 per beneficiary. 

This means that if the cost of a male goat is INR 30,000, the farmer will receive a subsidy of INR 15,000. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of improved breeds of goats. 

The improved breeds are expected to have better growth rates and higher reproductive efficiency. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a small or marginal farmer. 

The definition of small farmers is those with landholdings of up to 1 hectare. 

Marginal farmers are defined as those with landholdings of up to 2 hectares. 

Applicants must also be engaged in goat rearing or have a genuine interest in starting goat farming. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for the scheme. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Interested farmers must first approach the local animal husbandry department. 

They need to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the department office. 

The application form requires details such as the farmer's name, address, and landholding details. 

Farmers must also provide proof of their status as small or marginal farmers. 

This can include land records or any relevant documentation. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the local authorities. 

The verification process typically takes about 15 to 30 days. 

After verification, eligible farmers will be informed about the subsidy approval. 

The approved beneficiaries will then be required to purchase the male goats from authorized breeders. 

The government has a list of approved breeders to ensure quality. 

Farmers must retain the purchase receipt as it is required for subsidy disbursement. 

The subsidy amount is released directly to the beneficiary's bank account. 

This process usually takes about 15 days after the purchase is made. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the department can be found on the official government website. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall development of the goat farming sector. 

It is also anticipated to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 100 crore for the implementation of this scheme. 

This budget is aimed at supporting the subsidy for male goats for the targeted beneficiaries. 

The scheme is part of the larger National Livestock Mission. 

The National Livestock Mission was launched in 2014 to promote sustainable development of livestock sector. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of animal health and nutrition. 

Farmers are encouraged to provide proper veterinary care and nutrition to their goats. 

Training programs are organized to educate farmers about best practices in goat rearing. 

These training sessions cover topics such as breeding, feeding, and disease management. 

The government also collaborates with various NGOs for effective implementation of the scheme. 

These NGOs assist in reaching out to potential beneficiaries and providing necessary training. 

The scheme is expected to have a multiplier effect on the rural economy. 

By improving livestock quality, farmers can increase their income levels significantly. 

The demand for goat meat is consistently high in India. 

This presents a lucrative opportunity for farmers engaged in goat rearing. 

The scheme also aims to empower women farmers who are often engaged in livestock rearing. 

Women are encouraged to take part in goat farming as a means of income generation. 

The government has also introduced measures to ensure the sustainability of goat farming practices. 

This includes promoting organic farming methods and reducing the use of chemicals. 

The scheme is regularly monitored to assess its impact on the livelihoods of beneficiaries. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme further. 

The government aims to scale up the scheme based on its success in initial phases. 

Regular updates and reports are published to keep stakeholders informed. 

The scheme is seen as a vital step towards achieving self-sufficiency in meat production. 

It aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

Overall, the Scheme for Supply of Male Goat on Subsidy Basis is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses multiple facets of livestock farming and rural development. 

The scheme is designed to be inclusive and accessible to the most vulnerable farmers. 

With the right implementation and support, it has the potential to transform goat farming in India. 

This initiative reflects the government's commitment to improving the agricultural sector. 

It aims to create a sustainable livelihood for farmers through enhanced livestock productivity. 

The scheme is a testament to the importance of livestock in rural economies. 

It underscores the need for targeted interventions to support small and marginal farmers. 

In conclusion, the Scheme for Supply of Male Goat on Subsidy Basis represents a significant effort. 

It seeks to empower farmers while promoting sustainable agricultural practices in India.
